run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T23:40:09Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by a burst of failed frontend→ad gRPC GetAds calls. In sampled frontend error spans the GetAds client call fails with gRPC status 14 and the exact message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080'; 100.70.197.56:8080 is the ad Service ClusterIP. The frontend /api/data route and its incoming GET return HTTP 500 with the same error, and frontend-proxy's ingress spans inherit the failure (10-minute frontend-proxy ingress ERROR increase peaked at 430.53 at 23:50:09 and was back to 4.48 by 00:00:09). The ad Deployment was rollout-restarted at 2026-11-17T23:41:29Z (new ReplicaSet annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt, container template otherwise identical); the replacement ad pod was marked Ready at 23:41:31 and added to the Service endpoints, but its application logged 'Ad service starting.' only at 23:46:18 and 'Ad service started, listening on 8080' at 23:48:14, so traffic sent to its endpoint was refused until it listened. Ad's own GetAds server spans were absent (zero per-minute) during 23:45–23:50 and frontend GetAds errors stopped from 23:52. ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config currently has the fault setting adFailure (description 'Fail ad service') set to 'on' with all other fault flags off; no other object was seen applying a fault to ad, but the declared flag-driven fault itself was not observed (ad returned no error statuses, it simply received nothing), and the moment adFailure was switched on cannot be dated. Because of that, and because the trigger of the ad rollout restart is unknown (change_history is not integrated), the conclusion is partial. A separate low-rate stream of frontend-proxy HTTP 503 ingress spans already existed before 23:41 (23:35:33–23:40:31) and its cause was not identified.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own ERROR span counts deviated in two steps: 10-minute increase of ingress ERROR spans was 0 at 23:20:09, 2.17 at 23:25:09, 2.11 at 23:30:09 and 23:35:09, 6.32 at 23:40:09, then 188.42 at 23:45:09, 430.53 at 23:50:09, 250.53 at 23:55:09 and 4.48 at 00:00:09; the same service's 'router frontend egress' ERROR series was 0 through 23:40:09 and 176.84 / 408.42 / 231.58 at 23:45:09 / 23:50:09 / 23:55:09.

In the sampled frontend error spans (start times 23:48:17–23:48:43) the failing call is grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds with status tags otel.status_code=ERROR and rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and error detail '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080'; the parent 'executing api route (pages) /api/data', the 'GET /api/data' span and the outer 'GET' span carry http.status_code=500 and otel.status_code=ERROR.
Service otel-demo/ad has clusterIP 100.70.197.56 with port 8080 (targetPort 8080), i.e. the refused address in the frontend error message is the ad Service virtual IP, not a pod IP.

Per-minute (2m increase) data shows frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds ERROR spans starting in the 23:43 bucket (65.3, then 140, 158.7, 53.5, 133.3, 152, 140, 86.7, 20) and returning to 0 from 23:52, while ad's own oteldemo.AdService/GetAds server spans fell to 1.33 at 23:44 and were 0 for 23:45–23:50, resuming at 74.43 at 23:51 and ~130/min afterwards.

The ad container's own log gives the startup timeline: 'Ad service starting.' at 2026-11-17T23:46:18.907Z and 'Ad service started, listening on 8080' at 2026-11-17T23:48:14.209Z, with the first ad request lines ('Targeted ad request received ...') only from 23:48:55 onwards and normal request handling thereafter; no error or exception line appears in the readable ad log.

Kubernetes events in namespace otel-demo record the ad rollout at 2026-11-17T23:41:29–23:41:31Z: pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc 'Stopping container ad' (Killing, 23:41:31), ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 SuccessfulDelete, new pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh Scheduled 23:41:29 / Created and Started 23:41:30–31, ReplicaSet ad-785b4464f5 SuccessfulCreate, and Deployment ad ScalingReplicaSet 'Scaled up replica set ad-785b4464f5 from 0 to 1' / 'Scaled down replica set ad-554b849958 from 1 to 0'.

The new ad ReplicaSet's pod template differs from the old one only by the annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T23:41:29Z; both templates use image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad, container port 8080, env AD_PORT=8080 and the same resource limits (cpu 50m, memory 450Mi), and the container spec contains no readiness or liveness probe.

The replacement pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh (pod IP 100.96.3.224, restartCount 0, container running since 23:41:31Z) already had condition Ready=True with lastTransitionTime 23:41:31Z, and the ad Endpoints object lists that pod address 100.96.3.224:8080, so the pod was a Service endpoint while its application had not yet bound port 8080 (listening per its log only at 23:48:14).

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) currently sets adFailure with defaultVariant 'on', description 'Fail ad service', state ENABLED; adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure all have defaultVariant 'off'.

ad is the only otel-demo Deployment whose generation changed: Deployment ad is at generation 2 with 1/1 ready and condition NewReplicaSetAvailable lastUpdateTime 23:41:31Z, while Deployments frontend and frontend-proxy remain at generation 1 with their original ReplicaSets.

Before 23:41 a separate low-rate error stream existed on frontend-proxy itself: sampled ingress spans at 23:35:33, 23:37:03, 23:38:10 and 23:40:31 have error=true, http.status_code=503 while their child 'router frontend egress' spans carry error="true", http.status_code="0", and the corresponding load-generator GET spans are 503, with successful 200 spans interleaved in the same traces.

In the per-service ERROR-span query, error series were returned as zero for frontend POST, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, GET /api/cart, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, accounting 'orders receive', payment GET/dns.lookup/tcp.connect and ad flagd ResolveBoolean; frontend's only elevated error operations were GET /api/data (via 'executing api route (pages) /api/data') and grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, with frontend-proxy ingress and router frontend egress mirroring them.

The ad service's own spans never carry an error status: oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, getAdsByCategory, getRandomAds and resolve appear only with STATUS_CODE_UNSET, and the only ERROR-status ad series is flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream at ~1.05 per 10 minutes.

fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-zzt65 restarted once before the deviation: its container's last termination was OOMKilled with exitCode 137, startedAt 23:11:05Z and finishedAt 23:16:07Z, restartCount 1, current container running since 23:16:07Z; the frontend container frontend-675fd7b5c5-x27kw has restartCount 0 and has been running since 23:09:28Z.

The registered target exposes only two metric families in the queried window, traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket, so container CPU throttling and similar resource signals were not available for this investigation.

Root cause candidate: ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config holds the enabled fault setting adFailure ('Fail ad service', defaultVariant 'on') for the ad service, which is exactly the workload that was restarted at 23:41:29Z with an unchanged pod template (only kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt added) and that stopped receiving traffic during the error burst; no other Kubernetes object was observed applying a change or fault to ad. This cannot be closed because the ad service never returned a flag-driven error (it received no requests) and the time adFailure became 'on' is unknown.

Mechanism candidate: the 23:41:29Z ad rollout killed the serving pod and the replacement pod, having no readiness probe, was published as a Ready Service endpoint at 23:41:31 while its JVM needed until 23:48:14 to listen on 8080; connections to the ad ClusterIP 100.70.197.56:8080 were therefore refused between roughly 23:43 and 23:48–23:51, the frontend's GetAds calls failed with gRPC 14, /api/data returned HTTP 500 and frontend-proxy ingress errors spiked until the ad app finished starting. What issued the rollout restart itself was not found.

The alert may have fired on the earlier, low-rate frontend-proxy 503 stream (sampled at 23:35:33–23:40:31) rather than on the ad-driven burst, because the alert is reported as starting at 23:40:09Z with a very small 'current' value while the large ad-related burst only appears in the 23:45:09 and later 10-minute buckets; the rule expression is unavailable, so which errors crossed the threshold is unverified.

The ad service was not observed returning errors: its GetAds server spans are STATUS_CODE_UNSET only and it produced no GetAds spans at all during 23:45–23:50, so the observed failures happened before requests reached ad (client-side connect refusal) rather than being ad application error responses.

fraud-detection's OOM kill and restart is not the cause of this alert: it occurred at 23:16:07Z, before the error deviation and before the alert start, its own error-status series are zero apart from the persistent ~1.05/10m flagd EventStream series, and the frontend's elevated errors are confined to the /api/data → AdService/GetAds path with no checkout/cart path errors.

frontend-proxy itself was not the failing component: its ingress ERROR spans mirror child 'router frontend egress' upstream failures (http.status_code 0 in the early 503s and the same counts as frontend/GetAds errors in the burst), and its pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-kxdcl has been Running with restarts 0 since 23:09:23Z.

Add a readinessProbe (gRPC/HTTP on port 8080) to the ad container so a starting JVM is not published as a Service endpoint, and review the ad container's 50m CPU limit, which is the plausible reason its startup took ~6.7 minutes (container start 23:41:31 → listening 23:48:14).

Confirm whether flagd flag adFailure should be 'on' for this demo environment and correlate the ConfigMap change and the kubectl rollout restart of Deployment ad at 23:41:29Z with cluster audit/change history (the change_history integration is not available in this Run).

gaps: The alerting rule named RequestErrorRate was not returned by list_prometheus_rules (query for rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no_data, so it is unknown whether the rule exists in this Prometheus, what its expression/threshold is, and what the reported 'current: 2.4555' measures).

The change_history integration is not integrated, so the actor and command that produced the ad Deployment rollout restart (annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T23:41:29Z) could not be identified.

The timing of the flagd adFailure change is unknown: the flagd pod's logs returned no readable lines in 23:35–23:50 and the ConfigMap carries only creationTimestamp 2026-11-17T23:09:22Z, so it cannot be dated or shown that the setting caused the restart.

The declared fault (ad service failing because of the adFailure flag) was not observed happening: during the outage ad produced no GetAds spans and no error statuses, so the link between the flag and the observed connect refusals is unverified.
frontend container logs contained no readable lines in 23:20–00:04 (lines_read 0), so the frontend-side error output could not be read; only the trace error details were available.

The cause of the pre-existing low-rate frontend-proxy HTTP 503 ingress errors (sampled 23:35:33–23:40:31, with child egress spans at http.status_code 0) was not identified; no frontend restarts or error-status series explain it, and frontend logs were unavailable.

No samples exist before 23:20:09 in the queried metric views, so whether any of these signals were stable earlier is unknown rather than zero; trace span counts are not request counts and the trace views are biased samples.
No container CPU throttling or resource metrics exist on this target (only traces_span_metrics_* were listed), so whether the 50m CPU limit caused the ~6.7 minute ad startup lag is unchecked.
next_steps: Check cluster audit logs / CI-GitOps history for a kubectl rollout restart or patch of Deployment ad at 2026-11-17T23:41:29Z.
Use the flagd UI/flagd service logs or ConfigMap history to determine when adFailure was switched to 'on' and by whom.
Inspect the RequestErrorRate rule definition in the monitoring stack to verify which window and ratio produced 'current: 2.4555'.
Review the ad Deployment manifest (readiness probe, 50m CPU limit) and the frontend-proxy/frontend availability during ad restarts.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
